tooltip.title: Treatment of Alopecia Areata
tooltip.markdown: Therapy is stratified by the extent and severity of disease.

tooltip.title: Treatment for Limited AA (<50% Scalp Involvement)
tooltip.markdown: Focus is on localized anti-inflammatory treatments.

tooltip.title: Intralesional Corticosteroids
tooltip.markdown: The first-line treatment for patchy AA. Injections of triamcinolone acetonide are given directly into the alopecic patches every 4-6 weeks.

tooltip.title: Topical Therapies for AA
tooltip.markdown:
-   **High-Potency Steroids:** Can be used alone or between injection sessions.
-   **Topical Minoxidil:** May help stimulate and maintain regrowth.

tooltip.title: Treatment for Severe AA (≥50% Scalp, Totalis, Universalis)
tooltip.markdown: Requires systemic therapy to address widespread autoimmune activity.

tooltip.title: Oral Janus Kinase (JAK) Inhibitors
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Mechanism:** Target the cytokine signaling pathway (IFN-gamma, IL-15) that drives the disease.
-   **Baricitinib (Olumiant):** FDA-approved for severe AA in adults.
-   **Ritlecitinib (Litfulo):** FDA-approved for severe AA in adults and adolescents 12+.
-   **Tofacitinib/Ruxolitinib:** Used effectively off-label.

tooltip.title: Contact Immunotherapy
tooltip.markdown: Application of a potent contact allergen (like DPCP) to the scalp to induce a mild allergic reaction, which is thought to displace the autoimmune response.

tooltip.title: Traditional Systemic Immunosuppressants
tooltip.markdown: Agents like methotrexate or cyclosporine may be considered but have been largely superseded by the efficacy and specificity of JAK inhibitors.
